headline: Scarlet, a London-founded company designated to certify AI medical devices for Europe and the UK, has raised $50 million in a Series B funding round led by Headline.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a funded certifier aimed at a known approval bottleneck for AI medical devices, but the speed-up is the company's own claim.
importance_line: Makers of AI medical devices, and eventually the patients waiting for them, could see faster approvals in Europe and the UK if Scarlet's claim holds, but the saving of a year or more is the company's own figure and regulators, not Scarlet, set the rules.
summary: Wowtale reports that Scarlet, which holds official designation as a Notified Body (an organisation authorised to certify medical devices) under European Union rules and as an Approved Body under UK rules, closed a $50 million Series B round led by Headline, bringing its total funding to about $75 million. Scarlet claims its clients save at least a year on certifying new AI-enabled devices, a company claim given without independent figures, and it plans to use the money to expand its team of experts and its presence in the US and Asia-Pacific.
notes: Full Wowtale text read. Funding and speed figures come from the company as relayed by Wowtale.
